Subject: HelixHealth deployment guardrails — follow-up & qualification

Hi Laura — thanks again for your time earlier. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size the right deployment option (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) and address your isolation/SLO concerns.

Recap (from our call)
- Primary workload: clinical QA assistant + summarization for clinician notes (batch and streaming).
- Peak pattern: occasional spikes during end-of-day ingest, smaller sustained background traffic.
- Regulatory note: PHI may appear in inputs for some workflows.

Clarifying questions (to help recommend a path):
1) Target latency SLOs (p50/p95) for real-time clinician flows?
2) Expected peak concurrent QPS and sustained token throughput in estimates (ballpark ok).
3) Any contractual requirement for tenant isolation or dedicated hardware (e.g., must not share GPUs with other customers)?
4) Procurement timeline for Dedicated/Private (some customers need 60–90 days for procurement).

Our initial read: if PHI will be frequent and you need strict hardware isolation, Private VPC or on-prem will be safest. If you need predictable throughput and lower unit cost but still want strong isolation, Dedicated GPU pools with customer tenancy and dedicated node reservations are usually the sweet spot. Hosted API remains viable if you can accept logical isolation + strong contractual controls and SOC2 attestation.

Proposed next steps
- Can you confirm p95 latency target and a ballpark peak QPS?
- I'll loop in Aditya for a 60-minute technical deep-dive to go over isolation boundaries, caching, autoscaling, and SLO enforcement. Suggested times: Thu 3/18 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 3/19 09:00–10:00 PT.
- I attached a blank security questionnaire and a draft SOW to speed procurement.

Attachments: Helix_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx, Helix_Redwood_SOW_draft.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to locking down the right path.

Marissa — thanks for the summary and the materials. Answers inline below.

Q1 (latency): Our real-time clinician flows need p95 < 200ms for short prompts (~256 tokens). For long-form summarization we can tolerate higher latency (p95 < 3s).
Q2 (throughput): Ballpark peak during EOD: 120 QPS (short calls). Sustained: ~12 QPS. Token throughput variable — estimate ~8M tokens/day to start.
Q3 (isolation): We prefer no co-located GPUs with other tenants for PHI-exposed workloads. If a segmentation claim can be contractually backed and you provide dedicated pools, that would be acceptable.
Q4 (procurement): We target contract signature by end of Q2 2027; procurement/legal require SOC2 + customer-specific security questionnaire.

We are leaning Dedicated but need technical assurance on noisy-neighbor risk and an SLA for latency and availability. Happy to schedule the deep-dive. Thu 3/18 10am PT works for our infra lead.

Laura Chen

Nice summary, Marissa / Laura — a couple of pragmatic notes from a sales/ops perspective:

- Given the 120 QPS peak and p95 <200ms requirement, Dedicated with reserved GPU capacity is the most straightforward path. It eliminates noisy-neighbor risk by reserving whole nodes/pools for Helix.
- For PHI workloads, recommend Dedicated core pool + optional Private VPC for specific namespaces that must be air-gapped (we can hybridize: Dedicated + Private VPC for the strictest flows).
- Proposed SLA targets to propose in commercial: 99.95% availability for Dedicated, and an explicit latency SLO tied to reserved node sizing (we'll map #GPUs -> p95 for your target prompt length).
- Procurement: I'll prepare two commercial options: (A) Dedicated reserved (30/60/90-day ramp), (B) Dedicated + Private VPC add-on (higher TCO but meets strict isolation).

Next: Aditya — can you prepare a 1-page tech note on how Dedicated node reservation prevents noisy neighbor issues (high-level: GPU allocation, single-tenant kernels, KV/prefix cache isolation, QoS throttles) and a sizing recommendation for 120 QPS? If we have that, I can attach it to the commercial package.

Marissa / Ben / Laura — quick technical clarifications before the deep-dive. I'll bring a short deck. High level answers:

1) Isolation and noisy-neighbor mitigation (Dedicated):
- Dedicated GPU pools allocate whole GPU nodes to a customer namespace. Workloads run in single-tenant containers with dedicated kernel/execution paths. That means no other customer kernels execute on the same GPU instance, eliminating traditional noisy-neighbor burst interference.
- We enforce KV cache and prefix cache isolation per namespace; cache eviction policies are namespace-scoped so your active sessions won't be impacted by other tenants' traffic.

2) Private VPC / on-prem tradeoffs:
- Private VPC gives you full network control and customer-managed KMS; on-prem is available if you need physical separation. Both add ops overhead and slower rollout cadence.

3) Autoscaling, SLOs, and fallbacks:
- Autoscaling for Dedicated supports target-based scaling (QPS or token throughput) with warm pools to hit p95 targets. For guaranteed p95 <200ms we recommend a conservative warm-buffer (10–20% over baseline) during high variance periods.
- We support automatic fallback policies: if Dedicated pool is saturated, requests can fail-over to a pre-agreed hosted-variant (with different SLA/latency) — useful as a safety valve.

4) Sizing guidance (quick):
- For Helix's pattern (120 peak QPS short prompts): estimated starting reservation = 8 x A100-class GPUs with batching tuned for 256-token prompts. I'll validate in the deep-dive with real prompt samples.

5) Proposed agenda for Thu 3/18 (60 mins):
- 0–10m: Introductions & objectives
- 10–25m: Workload profile deep-dive (Laura/infra lead show samples)
- 25–45m: Isolation architecture: Dedicated vs Private VPC (we'll show metrics/benchmarks)
- 45–55m: SLA mapping & sizing (Ben/Aditya present draft numbers)
- 55–60m: Action items & procurement timeline

Attachments: redwood-tenant-isolation.pdf (one-pager), will also drop a small sizing worksheet in the Drive folder.

See you Thu 10:00 PT.
